learn.hook: Is 500 BCE older or newer than 200 BCE? Counting time in history has a fun twist!
points: A timeline shows events in the order in which they happened, from earlier to later.
Most of the world today counts years using the Common Era. Years after the start of this count are written CE (Common Era); years before it are written BCE (Before Common Era).
Earlier, the same years were called AD and BC. CE is the same as AD, and BCE is the same as BC.
BCE years count backwards: 500 BCE came before 200 BCE. CE years count forwards: 200 CE came before 500 CE. There is no year zero; 1 BCE is followed directly by 1 CE.
A decade is 10 years, a century is 100 years and a millennium is 1,000 years. The 21st century runs from 2001 to 2100.

example.q: Put these in order from oldest to newest: 300 CE, 600 BCE, 100 BCE, 1200 CE.
steps: BCE years are older than all CE years.
Among BCE years, the bigger number is older: 600 BCE, then 100 BCE.
Among CE years, the smaller number is older: 300 CE, then 1200 CE.

learn.reallife: Your birth year, the year your school was built and the year India became independent (1947) are all CE years you can put on your own family timeline.

quiz.q: What does CE stand for?
quiz.explain: CE means Common Era, the years counted forward in the system most of the world uses today.
steps: Years after the start of the count are written CE.
CE stands for Common Era.
Years before it are BCE (Before Common Era). Answer: Common Era
quiz.mistake: Guesses a phrase that just matches the letters

quiz.q: Which year came first?
quiz.explain: BCE years count backwards, so 500 BCE is earlier than 200 BCE, and all BCE years come before CE years.
steps: All BCE years come before CE years, so 100 CE and 300 CE are later.
BCE years count backwards: the bigger BCE number is earlier.
500 BCE is earlier than 200 BCE. Answer: 500 BCE
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger BCE number means a later year

quiz.q: How many years are there in a century?
quiz.explain: A century is 100 years; a decade is 10 and a millennium is 1,000.
steps: Decade = 10 years, century = 100 years, millennium = 1,000 years.
Answer: 100
quiz.mistake: Mixes up century, decade and millennium

quiz.q: India became independent in 1947 and the Constitution came into force in 1950. How many years apart are these events?
quiz.mistake: Makes a subtraction slip
steps: Later year − earlier year
= 3 years
Answer: 3

quiz.q: A pot was made in 500 BCE and a coin in 200 BCE. How many years older is the pot?
quiz.explain: Both dates are BCE. Count back: 500 − 200 = 300, so the pot is 300 years older.
quiz.mistake: Adds BCE years instead of subtracting
steps: Both years are BCE
The pot is older because 500 BCE is earlier
Answer: 300

quiz.q: In which century is the year 2026?
quiz.explain: The 21st century covers the years 2001 to 2100, so 2026 is in it.
steps: The 21st century runs from 2001 to 2100.
2026 lies between 2001 and 2100.
So 2026 is in the 21st century (not the 20th, which ends in 2000).
Answer: 21st century
quiz.mistake: Uses the first two digits (20) as the century number

quiz.q: Which year comes just after 1 BCE?
quiz.explain: There is no year zero, so the count goes straight from 1 BCE to 1 CE.
steps: There is no year zero.
1 BCE is followed directly by 1 CE.
Answer: 1 CE
quiz.mistake: Assumes there is a year zero

quiz.q: BC and AD are older names. Which pair means the same?
quiz.explain: BCE is the same as BC, and CE is the same as AD; only the names changed.
steps: Older names: BC and AD.
BCE is the same as BC; CE is the same as AD.
Answer: BCE = BC and CE = AD
quiz.mistake: Swaps the matching pairs

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled. 'How can 300 BCE be older than 100 BCE? Bigger numbers should be newer!'
teach.praise: Ahaa! BCE years count backwards, so 300 BCE came before 100 BCE, and all BCE years come before CE years. Timelines are fun!
teach.nudge: What happens to the counting of BCE years? Do they go up or down as time goes on?

revise.summary: A timeline puts events in order from earlier to later. Years after the start of the Common Era are CE and years before it are BCE; BCE counts backwards and there is no year zero.
focus: Ordering BCE and CE years on a timeline
Meaning of CE and BCE and their older names AD and BC
No year zero: 1 BCE is followed by 1 CE
Decade, century, millennium and which century a year is in
remember: CE = Common Era = AD; BCE = Before Common Era = BC
BCE counts backwards: 500 BCE is before 200 BCE
traps: Don't think a bigger BCE number is later; it is earlier
2026 is in the 21st century, not the 20th

learn.hook: How do we know what people ate 2,000 years ago, when nobody had cameras? Historians are like detectives!
points: Historians find out about the past using sources, which are clues left behind from earlier times.
Archaeological sources are objects: tools, pots, beads, toys, coins, bones, buildings and paintings.
Written (literary) sources include manuscripts, handwritten long ago on palm leaves or the bark of the birch tree, and inscriptions, writings carved on stone or metal.
Oral traditions are songs, stories and sayings passed down by word of mouth from one generation to the next.
Historians compare many sources, check them carefully and then build a picture of what happened.

example.q: A copper coin is found with a king's name and picture on it. What can a historian learn from it?
steps: The name tells us who ruled.
The picture and words show the language and art of that time.
Where the coin is found shows how far trade or the kingdom reached.
example.answer: The ruler's name, the language and art of that time, and clues about trade.

learn.reallife: Old family photos, your grandmother's recipes and the stories she tells are sources of your own family's history!

quiz.q: What is a source in history?
options: Any clue that tells us about the past
quiz.explain: Objects, writings and oral stories from the past are all sources.
steps: Sources are clues left behind from earlier times.
They include objects, writings and oral traditions.
Answer: Any clue that tells us about the past
quiz.mistake: Thinks only textbooks count as sources

quiz.q: What is a manuscript?
options: A text written by hand long ago
quiz.explain: Manuscripts were handwritten, often on palm leaves or birch bark.
steps: Written sources include manuscripts and inscriptions.
A manuscript was handwritten long ago, on palm leaves or birch bark.
A carving on rock is an inscription. Answer: A text written by hand long ago
quiz.mistake: Confuses manuscripts with inscriptions

quiz.q: Which of these is an inscription?
options: Words carved on a stone pillar
A story told by a grandmother
quiz.explain: Inscriptions are writings carved or engraved on hard surfaces like stone or metal.
steps: Inscriptions are writings carved on stone or metal.
Words carved on a stone pillar fit this.
A grandmother's story is oral; a clay toy is an object. Answer: Words carved on a stone pillar
quiz.mistake: Thinks any old object is an inscription

quiz.q: Songs and stories passed down by word of mouth are called what?
quiz.explain: 'Oral' means spoken; these sources are remembered and spoken, not written.
steps: 'Oral' means spoken.
Songs and stories passed by word of mouth are oral traditions.
Answer: Oral traditions
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'oral'

quiz.q: On which material were many old manuscripts written in India?
quiz.explain: Palm leaves and birch bark were common writing materials long ago.
steps: Manuscripts were handwritten long ago.
They were written on palm leaves or the bark of the birch tree.
Answer: Palm leaves
quiz.mistake: Picks a modern material

quiz.q: Which is an archaeological (object) source?
options: A clay pot dug up from an old site
quiz.explain: Archaeological sources are physical remains like pots, tools, coins and buildings.
steps: Archaeological sources are objects: tools, pots, coins, bones, buildings.
A clay pot dug up from an old site is an object.
A folk song is oral.
Answer: A clay pot dug up from an old site
quiz.mistake: Mixes up object sources with oral or modern sources

quiz.q: Why do historians use many sources instead of just one?
options: Because one source is always false
To check facts and get a fuller, more reliable picture
quiz.explain: Comparing sources helps historians cross-check information and fill gaps.
steps: Historians compare many sources and check them carefully.
This helps cross-check facts and fill gaps.
Answer: To check facts and get a fuller, more reliable picture
quiz.mistake: Thinks one source is enough to know the whole story

quiz.q: What could a historian learn from a coin with a king's name on it?
quiz.explain: Coins often carry rulers' names and symbols, which help date and identify kingdoms.
steps: A coin carries a king's name and picture.
So it tells us who ruled at that time.
It cannot tell the weather or dreams. Answer: Who ruled at that time
quiz.mistake: Expects sources to tell things they cannot show

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Nobody alive today saw ancient India. So how do we know anything about it?'
teach.praise: Now I see! Historians use clues called sources: objects like coins and pots, written texts like manuscripts and inscriptions, and oral stories!
teach.nudge: What kinds of clues do historians use? Can you name an object and a written one?

revise.summary: Historians learn about the past from sources: objects (archaeological), writings like manuscripts and inscriptions, and oral traditions. They compare and check many sources before building a picture.
focus: Types of sources: archaeological, written (literary) and oral
What objects like coins can tell us
remember: Source = clue left behind from earlier times
Manuscript = handwritten on palm leaves or birch bark
Inscription = writing carved on stone or metal
Oral traditions = songs, stories, sayings passed by word of mouth
traps: Don't mix up a manuscript (handwritten) with an inscription (carved)
A folk song is an oral source, not an archaeological one
Don't rely on one source; historians cross-check many

learn.hook: Imagine digging carefully in the soil and finding a toy that a child played with 4,000 years ago!
points: Archaeology is the study of the past through the objects and buildings people left behind.
Archaeologists dig carefully at old sites. This careful digging is called excavation.
Usually, objects in deeper layers of soil are older and those in upper layers are newer.
Scientists can test materials like bones, seeds and wood to find out roughly how old they are.
The rock shelters of Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh have very old rock paintings of animals and people. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

example.q: At a dig, an archaeologist finds a coin in the top layer and a stone tool in a much deeper layer. Which is probably older?
steps: Soil and remains pile up over time, one layer on top of another.
Deeper layers were laid down earlier.
So the stone tool from the deeper layer is probably older.

learn.reallife: When you visit a museum like the National Museum in New Delhi, many of the pots, seals and sculptures were found by archaeologists.

quiz.q: What is archaeology?
options: The study of the past using objects and remains people left
quiz.explain: Archaeologists learn about the past from tools, pots, bones, buildings and more.
steps: Archaeology studies the past through objects and buildings left behind.
Answer: The study of the past using objects and remains people left
quiz.mistake: Confuses archaeology with astronomy or botany

quiz.q: What is the careful digging of an old site called?
quiz.explain: Excavation means carefully digging and uncovering remains.
steps: Archaeologists dig carefully at old sites.
This careful digging is called excavation.
Answer: Excavation
quiz.mistake: Mixes up similar-sounding words

quiz.q: In an excavation, which layer usually has the oldest objects?
options: All layers have objects of the same age
quiz.explain: Layers pile up over time, so the bottom layers are usually the oldest.
steps: Soil layers pile up over time.
Deeper layers are usually older; upper layers newer.
Answer: The deepest layer
quiz.mistake: Thinks newer things sink to the bottom

quiz.q: Where are the famous Bhimbetka rock shelters?
quiz.explain: The Bhimbetka rock shelters are near Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh.
steps: The Bhimbetka rock shelters are in Madhya Pradesh.
They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Answer: Madhya Pradesh
quiz.mistake: Guesses a state without knowing

quiz.q: What can be seen on the walls of the Bhimbetka rock shelters?
options: Very old paintings of animals and people
quiz.explain: Early people painted animals, hunting scenes and dances on these rock walls.
steps: Bhimbetka has very old rock paintings.
They show animals and people.
Answer: Very old paintings of animals and people
quiz.mistake: Does not connect rock shelters with ancient paintings

quiz.q: Why do archaeologists dig slowly, often using small tools and brushes?
options: To make the work last longer
Because machines are not allowed anywhere
So that fragile objects are not broken
quiz.explain: Old pots and bones can break easily, so careful digging protects them.
steps: Old pots and bones are fragile.
Small tools and brushes avoid breaking them.
Answer: So that fragile objects are not broken
quiz.mistake: Does not see why care is needed

quiz.q: Which of these would an archaeologist most likely study?
options: A cricket score from last week
A broken pot from an ancient village
quiz.explain: Archaeologists study remains from the past, like pottery, tools and buildings.
steps: Archaeologists study remains from the past.
A broken pot from an ancient village is such a remain.
A new phone or last week's score is not from the past.
Answer: A broken pot from an ancient village
quiz.mistake: Thinks any object, even modern, is the focus of archaeology

quiz.q: How can scientists help archaeologists find the age of old bones or seeds?
options: By asking the oldest person in the village
quiz.explain: Scientific tests on materials like bones, seeds and wood help estimate their age.
steps: Scientists can test bones, seeds and wood.
These tests tell roughly how old they are.
Answer: By testing them in laboratories
quiz.mistake: Thinks dating is only guesswork

teach.ask: Gappu finds a broken pot in the garden. 'Is this treasure? How would an archaeologist study it?'
teach.praise: Wow! Archaeologists excavate carefully, layer by layer, and deeper layers usually hold older things. I'm a junior archaeologist now!
teach.nudge: How do archaeologists dig, and how can the layers of soil tell us which object is older?

revise.summary: Archaeology studies the past through objects and buildings people left behind, uncovered by careful digging called excavation. Deeper layers are usually older, and Bhimbetka's rock paintings are a famous example.

Bhimbetka rock shelters in Madhya Pradesh
